6663c246dcef8cafefaa: Prestige marks a character’s entry into the ranks of the greatest in their field. The experience accumulated during the voyage takes shape in abilities that make legendary feats possible. A blow can reshape the ground of a battlefield; in the hands of an exceptional swordsman, even an ordinary blade becomes a fearsome weapon. Aboard ship, the expertise of whoever holds the helm or tends the wounded can decide the fate of the entire crew.
5a1235e081c9368dc5de: This growth preserves the character’s identity. Someone who built their style on physical power continues to express it through strength. Someone who relies on movement, precision or specialist knowledge takes those qualities to ever greater heights. Prestige makes the path they have followed recognisable and lets them explore its possibilities to their peak.
e092ab5e18458f38b924: Every Role can achieve this excellence through its own craft. A carpenter expresses it in the ship they build and keep afloat. An archaeologist demonstrates it by reading what others cannot interpret. For a captain, it can mean leading the crew at a moment when a well-given order changes the outcome of the battle. Prestige feats also belong to those who make the voyage possible.
e79698d90fc28ee6a24c: In die-based progressions, Prestige continues growth beyond d20. The die retains the d20 and gains an additional die, which increases through six stages: d20+d4, d20+d6, d20+d8, d20+d10, d20+d12 and d20+d20. The first five are called Prestige I, II, III, IV and V; the sixth is named Saikyō. The larger scales are reached gradually as you progress towards this peak.
ef8e79eac3c8d0837838: This progression improves the relevant rolls and powers the effects that depend on the die reached. Where a rule uses the full roll, the additional die is also included. Where it specifies a distance, radius or another value linked to Prestige, use the scale of the ability concerned.
b461ce9e6d97bf4e1662: If the Racial Attribute enters Prestige, Passive Defence also continues to grow. PD uses the full Grade of the Racial Attribute: add together the maximum values of its component dice and add +1. No roll is made.
d368d48b71dd378e51c9: Talents, Techniques, Haki, Unique Traits and other effects that explicitly modify Passive Defence apply after calculating the base value.
dd5b31fd5510ef28435b: When a graded source that has reached Prestige imposes a Save, it does not roll its own pool. The Prestige Grade determines a fixed Threshold according to the following table. The target makes the Save with their full Attribute, including any Prestige die, and succeeds if the result meets or exceeds the Threshold.
20e940a1265562375c00: The Status determines the Save Attribute; the source determines the Threshold. Specific rules with their own Threshold or a different procedure still take precedence.
1546a2d1c0f6b8abecd4: When a Prestige Talent directly applies a Status and does not specify a different source, the Threshold comes from the current Grade of the Role Skill governing that Talent. This also applies to Statuses applied by evolutions, such as Unstoppable Maul and Seismic Wave. An effect included in a Technique instead uses the Technique’s Grade, unless a specific rule says otherwise.
ae797b2433725143734f: Each Attribute, Skill or Haki Colour retains its own progression. A character can excel in one area while still being a beginner in another. This combination defines their speciality.
1d29a45a5e7054745134: Attribute Prestige develops the qualities on which the character builds their feats. Strength can expand destruction and launches; Technique can support superhuman movement and agility; Cunning can take control of shots to exceptional levels. Additional benefits follow Role compatibility and the conditions of the ability used.
953ca80d7823ae8f8fc7: This is why two characters with the same Attribute can express Prestige in different ways. A Striker’s Strength manifests in impacts, while a Swordsman develops their ability to cleave through the Talents provided by their path. Technique mobility can belong to Striker and Swordsman; other Roles use the benefits compatible with their specialisation. The Attribute die nevertheless remains available for the normal rolls provided by the rules.
1019cdb7bf621575f811: Role Skill Prestige instead grants access to the Talents that make the abilities of a profession extraordinary. You acquire one Talent at d20+d4, a second at d20+d8 and a third at d20+d12. The order is free, subject to prerequisites. At Saikyō, your acquired Talents improve.
25b22c990ca9a6b2e038: The additional upgrades from Strength, Technique and Cunning do not consume these choices. Attribute and Skill can grow at different Grades: a high Attribute expands the possibilities that belong to it, while a high Skill opens choices from its catalogue. Sharing a Skill with another specialisation does not automatically grant its Talents.
60a909b7f8c358a740c3: Synergies between Attributes and Skills continue to be checked beyond d20. A Synergy can use any Skill allowed by its requirement, even if it is not a Role Skill. Intermediate Prestige Grades do not grant new Unique Traits and do not consume Role Skill Prestige Talent choices.
7ce0d5a456b72673f900: The full Synergy rules and the ordinary Unique Trait catalogue are provided in §16.9 of the Game Manual.
056010b37d44f3ebc906: Spirit Prestige develops the character’s determination and offers three upgrades shared by all Roles. Choices occur at d20+d4, d20+d8 and d20+d12. These abilities let you express your will through mental resistance, coordinated Colour activation and PIP recovery according to their respective rules.
9252aa7b04af9a74ff0e: Armament and Observation cannot exceed the Spirit die, including its Prestige. Spirit raises the attainable limit, while each Colour grows along its own path. Their Prestige upgrades existing active effects; ordinary passives retain their function. The pools retain their established maximums: 5 Armament PIP, 5 Observation PIP and 3 Conqueror’s PIP.
f9b095c624a734956836: The Sniper’s Observation Role Skill and Observation Haki remain two separate progressions.
283e28db06852fbd3f0d: Conqueror’s Haki follows a separate progression consisting of Prestige I, Prestige II and Saikyō. It has no die and requires no numerical Spirit thresholds. The GM assigns these stages in relation to the character’s development in the campaign.
42aacf574153ae7a9543: Prestige expands what a character can attempt and the effectiveness of acquired abilities. To use them, declare the intention and form of the intervention, then apply the relevant rules. Activations, reaches and use limits continue to guide choices during battle. Materials and preparation retain their importance in professional activities.
659713def2106acb731a: A large scale describes the possible scope of a feat. Actual destruction depends on the impact and the resilience of the environment; creatures are affected according to the attack or Talent used. Similarly, a legendary ship comes from work in a shipyard, and an extraordinary dish must actually be prepared. The ability to achieve exceptional results is expressed through specific actions.
552f28dd2fa655bb3513: Resources make these actions meaningful. Role Talents, Spirit upgrades and Haki effects share the normal availability of Bonus Actions. The player decides when to use their most powerful Talent, which abilities to accompany it with, and how many resources to keep for the next moment.
fc50db5e5ee8962f410c: Saikyō is the peak of a specific Prestige path. In die-based progressions it corresponds to d20+d20; for Conqueror’s Haki it is the third stage assigned by the GM. A character can reach it in their Role Skill while other areas continue to grow.
5055d31ce3caabb49fc4: At this level, already acquired Talents and upgrades reach their final form. Saikyō does not grant a fourth Talent. Ultimates retain their own rules: the system introduces no dedicated Prestige evolutions.
6d426bd143988b860fc9: Synergies have no Trait progression at individual Prestige Grades. When both the Attribute and Skill of the same Synergy reach Saikyō, that pair can make a single Prestige Unique Trait available. This Trait is not a fourth Role Talent and follows its own catalogue. Until that catalogue is published, reaching Saikyō does not automatically grant a new effect.
c980c27ec41028089204: The character continues to carry the choices that shaped them. Their abilities can now affect a battle, a crossing or the crew’s survival with a force that once seemed unreachable. Prestige allows those feats to be played and to become part of the story of their own voyage.
ad6501ee3216d92a076a: Prestige develops the character through two separate progressions. Attribute Prestige upgrades the abilities of compatible Roles and determines scales for destruction, launching, mobility, cutting, range and trajectory control. Role Skill Prestige grants the choices used to acquire the Prestige Talents of your Role.
a5fa0df7bf41e037f9a8: Attribute upgrades are gained on reaching the required threshold and do not consume Talent choices. Using them still requires a compatible ability, with its effects, slots, actions and costs. Skill Talents, however, are acquired individually: reaching a threshold does not grant the entire catalogue.
37a0652ad40c2135870f: The two progressions can be at different Grades. A high Attribute expands physical possibilities without granting Skill Talents; a high Skill grants choices without automatically raising Attribute scales. In this text, the Technique Attribute means the character’s characteristic; a Technique means a move built with its own effects and costs. ST means Stamina and SP means Structure Points.

cb65644b69748622e884: For the Swordsman, slash and cut scales can only be used after acquiring the respective Talents Sovereign Slash and Colossal Cut. Technique mobility is instead an Attribute upgrade available even without those Talents.
eca33dc297c7006338ca: The exclusions in the matrix concern only the additional upgrades described here. All Roles continue to use the Prestige die for normal Attribute rolls: a Sniper with Strength d20+d8 rolls d20+d8 normally, even if they do not have the destruction wave or Colossal Launch.
7e6b1f0243e197751085: The Crusher applies Strength benefits through attacks and Techniques compatible with their bludgeoning weapon. Striker Talents require the corresponding Role and their own prerequisites: using Athletics as a Role Skill does not grant them to the Crusher or Swordsman.
22eea5e0c4507ad8349d: The Swordsman retains their own form of destruction through cleaving: Strength does not grant them the radial environmental wave or Colossal Launch of Striker and Crusher. Sniper, Crusher and the other Roles excluded from mobility retain their ordinary movement effects. Any independent abilities from Race, Fruit or Haki follow their own rules.
b1ef1da8d8a269181f69: For Striker and Crusher, Strength in Prestige makes the environmental destruction scale and Colossal Launch available. They are passive Attribute upgrades, with an additional cost of 0 ST and no Talent choice. Destruction concerns a Strength-based impact or an ability that expressly uses its scale, such as the Striker’s Titanic Wave Talent and the Crusher’s Seismic Wave. Colossal Launch requires an offensive melee Technique of your own Role containing the Builder’s Launch effect. All costs of the Technique and effects used remain payable.
0d45f20dd67ff824878e: This only serves to distinguish it from the Striker’s Launch Talent and other abilities that produce their own push.
d907e0f2b137f1876194: These values are maximums. You may choose a shorter distance or a smaller radius. The destruction radius is measured from the impact point: a radius of 100 m corresponds to an area 200 m in diameter. At Saikyō, the radius of 1,000 m corresponds to a diameter of 2,000 m.
8767466550377c4f59ba: You do not roll Strength to determine how many metres you reach: use the row corresponding to its current die. The Strength roll is used when a rule requires a check or, in the case of Crash, to determine damage.
92b640f40f38bf288ae9: If Strength has not yet reached Prestige, the distances and sizes provided by ordinary effects remain in force. In particular, a Technique’s Launch effect retains its 3 m.
03e3ae065bbf931b2275: The destruction scale expresses the maximum extent of the environmental consequences of a Strength blow: broken paving, gouged ground, torn-off doors, shattered cover and damaged parts of structures. The impact point is the centre of the area.
32a06db43cc285f6362d: The radius indicates how far the devastation can extend. Actual destruction depends on the blow, material, resilience of the obstacle and damage dealt. A strong wall can remain standing even if it lies within the maximum area. The scale does not automatically destroy every object in the area.
f78624684203b9dbc3ba: For structures with Structure Points, abbreviated SP, subtract the damage actually suffered and apply the specified consequences when they give way. For elements without SP, the GM determines breakage and collapse consistent with the damage and material. When an impact propagates through the area, damage decreases with distance according to the following bands.
7291f45b73269bf4bdbe: For Striker and Crusher the scale limits the consequences for the environment; the blow or effect used determines which targets receive numerical damage. Dealing the blow’s damage to creatures in an area requires the Striker’s Titanic Wave Talent, the Crusher’s Seismic Wave or a Technique that provides for it. Prestige Strength alone does not assign damage to all creatures within the radius.
48b2c4c85e8800131052: A Crash can also produce cracks, debris and breakage compatible with this scale. Its damage remains as established by Colossal Launch and is applied only to the recipients specified in the first collision rule.
bd4a4fbe5b6af1354298: Type: passive Strength Attribute upgrade. Roles: Striker and Crusher. Requirement: Strength of at least d20+d4 and a compatible impact on the environment. Additional cost: 0 ST. Additional action: none.
beae3f68c5bf43128a89: You may use the scale when you land a Strength-based attack and the impact is actually delivered to the ground, an object or a structure. It can be a basic attack or an offensive Technique of your Role: a Striker can punch the ground; a Crusher can bring their hammer down on the floor or against a wall. For the Crusher, the attack must use a compatible bludgeoning weapon.
fe56173a9fc218d23765: A blow against a creature can also affect the environment if the impact is transmitted to a surface or structure. Identify the contact that produces the devastation: hitting an opponent backed against a wall, delivering the blow into the ground beneath them, or making them collide with a surface through the specified effects. Simply hitting a creature does not automatically damage the entire surrounding environment.
826d5843703802963427: The scale expresses the ability to extend an actual impact. A missed or avoided blow does not automatically produce an area of damage. If a collision with the environment nevertheless occurs during resolution, that collision must be recognised and resolved with its own damage; it is not assumed to have occurred merely because Strength is in Prestige.
91ade419948cc811b5a6: Environmental destruction alone does not require acquiring a Skill Prestige Talent, and does not require Launch or Crash in the Technique. These effects become necessary when you want to hurl a creature and deal the collision damage described in the following sections. A normal Strength check to lift, drag or push an object does not automatically deal the damage of an attack.
149afd7cc887b9f243dc: Before rolling, declare the point you want to hit and, if you want to propagate devastation, the chosen extent within your Strength’s maximum radius. Resolve the attack with its normal reach, required actions and any Technique costs. An undefended surface requires no additional check to activate the upgrade; any rolls needed to reach or hit it follow the ordinary rules.
966f4b1d9b6e7ed275e0: When the impact occurs, use the blow’s damage as D and apply to the structures reached the band for their distance from the impact point. For a Crash, instead use only its Strength roll, respecting the limit on recipients of the first collision. Do not make an additional Strength roll to determine the radius or add environmental damage that is not provided for.
fbdb50b4dd4c15e3e37c: For structures with SP, subtract the actual damage after the relevant reductions. The Crusher’s Demolisher and the Striker’s Breaking Fists, if acquired, retain their benefits against compatible objects; attenuation bands continue to apply. For elements without SP the GM determines consequences consistent with the damage and material.
106850832944d78aba75: The impact must be able to reach the elements involved: an obstacle that withstands it can stop its propagation. The maximum radius does not guarantee that every structure in the area breaks. You may choose a smaller extent, and a particular ability can define the zone differently, such as the cone of Seismic Wave.

432ae98bfd5fa3bc0bd1: Environmental destruction alone applies propagated damage to the environment. Creatures receive the attack’s direct damage only if they are targets of the ability used. Collapses, falls and other hazards produced by the breaking environment can still injure them under the normal environmental rules; they are not an automatic copy of the punch or hammer damage.
6c718ab333466db7ce8d: A Striker with the Titanic Wave Talent may, after a successful blow of their own on their turn, spend the Bonus Action and 2 ST to also strike the other creatures in the chosen radial area. A Crusher with Seismic Wave may, after a Strength bludgeoning blow with valid contact on the environment on their turn, spend the Bonus Action and 3 ST to attack the creatures resting on the surface in the chosen cone. Both use the same Strength scale, with the limits and defences described in their respective Talents.
fc8cc4adb5a2ffd49727: A Talent or Technique granting an area attack also determines which creatures you hit. The Strength scale does not automatically enlarge the area of any Technique: a move must expressly reference this scale to use it against creatures. Its actions, effects, slots and costs remain necessary.
6514cb781a55a559f179: Structures reached by the same impact receive the damage for their band only once. The passive scale and the Talent propagating that blow do not generate two copies of damage on the same object or creature.
d95a72d9d4d269e2db12: Striker example: with Strength d20+d10 you strike the ground and deal 40 damage. The maximum radius is 100 m. Paving at 40 m may receive 20 environmental damage, according to its resilience and SP; a guard at that distance does not automatically receive that 20 damage. If, after the blow, you activate Titanic Wave by paying the Bonus Action and 2 ST, the guard reached by the wave may defend: if hit, they also receive the 20 damage specified by their band. The paving does not receive another 20 damage from the second description of the same impact.
